title: Simplification, clean re-test of 189-fable on the 191-claude incumbent: delete the pretraining-only MTP module (136-fable); plain next-token loss, identical handoff model (9,557,760 params), -48 lines
description: Idea ID: P50-family ablation (the 136-fable multi-token-prediction objective), under program.md's simplification focus, as the fresh registration that 189-fable's record names as its next step: pretrain.py is 191-claude's with MTP_WEIGHT, class MTPHead, mtp_loss and the trunk's features() split deleted (189's pretrain.patch applied unchanged; it applies cleanly), so pretraining minimises the fork's loss_on (next-token cross-entropy on proof tokens) alone, while the model, optimizers, no-warmup schedule, init rule, token batches, compile recipe and handoff are untouched. 189 produced no valid 3-seed mean because each of its two attempts lost one seed to infrastructure (no A40 capacity; a pod whose Lean gate ran ~5x slow), although its four finished seed-runs scored 678/695/680/700, so whether expert iteration needs the module at width 384 is still open; if it does not, the incumbent loses 48 lines and gains ~20% pretraining steps that a later larger or looped model can spend. The only open registration is 192-claude (lean-no-peri-ln), a different simplification (the Peri-LN branch-output LayerNorms), so this does not duplicate it.
hypothesis: MTP's +11.7 was measured once, at width 256 and 3,370 steps (136 vs 129). Since then the model doubled in parameters and pretraining reached ~4.7 epochs, and 189's four finished seed-runs without the module (on the 186 base, with warmup) averaged 688.3 against 186's 680.3, with expert iteration closing a weaker round-1 start by round 4 (RL-solved 1,155-1,194 vs 1,159-1,193). Reading (b) of 189: at this size the t+2 objective shapes the zero-shot sampler (held-out greedy 0.952 vs 0.974, round-1 targets solved 482 vs 743 on average) but not what four rounds of expert iteration reach, so the module is dead weight for the metric. Risk this run tests: 190 and 191 showed that early-trajectory changes (init, warmup) also weaken round 1 (191: 682/454/225 targets), and 188 showed a seed can fail to bootstrap from a thin round-1 harvest (307 -> 282 eval); 191 already removed the warmup, so this candidate stacks two round-1-weakening simplifications and could lose a seed to a collapse that neither showed alone. Per seed the data order (both generators) and the embedding/readout initialisation equal 191's; the trunk's orthogonal matrices do not (191 builds the MTP module before the orthogonal-init loop, which shifts the global RNG), so paired seed differences are ordinary seed pairs. Decision rule fixed now, the same tolerance 189/190/191 registered for their simplifications: keep if the 3-seed mean is >= 680.33, i.e. strictly above 191's 683.67 or within 3.33 of it (program.md's '~0 with less code'); below 680.33 discard. If the other agent keeps a file first, record.py's rule applies.
expected_delta: -40 to +25 vs 191's 683.7 (central 0); keep needs a 3-seed mean >= 680.33 (rule in the hypothesis). Pretraining 6,300-6,800 steps in 300 s per seed (central 6,550; bench below: first step at 25 s, then 24.2 steps/s; 189 measured 6,316-6,710 on five pods; 191: 5,362/5,298/5,220), 5.6-6.0 epochs at ~1,132 batches per epoch; final val loss 0.075-0.092, last train loss 0.03-0.055; held-out greedy after pretraining 0.91-0.975 (189: 0.915-0.969; 191: 0.959-0.972); round-1 RL targets solved 150-720 (189: 178-716; 191: 225-682) and round-4 RL-solved 1,130-1,200; handoff n_params 9,557,760 exactly; RL sampling 160-290 samples/s (handoff model unchanged), totals 1,650-2,100 s of 2,400. Falsifiers: mean steps < 6,000 (the module cost less than measured); a 3-seed mean below 660, or any seed whose round-4 RL-solved stays below 900, says the module (or its interaction with no-warmup) still matters at width 384; a mean >= 680.33 says it is not needed.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, the 191-claude handoff model unchanged; ALiBiGPT.forward is again one method (the features() split existed only to feed the MTP module)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 191-claude: deleted MTP_WEIGHT, class MTPHead, mtp_loss and ALiBiGPT.features (folded back into forward, same computation); pretrain() no longer builds, compiles, initialises, clips or optimises an MTP module and calls the fork's loss_on; curve points no longer carry mtp_loss. 9 insertions, 57 deletions (pretrain.py 428 -> 380 lines); the diff is 189-fable's pretrain.patch applied to 191's file. Widths, depth, heads, ALiBi slopes, Muon/AdamW, no-warmup wall-clock cosine, init rule, token batches (TOK_BUDGET 18,432), per-block compile, CUDA-graphed Muon step and handoff unchanged.
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760, identical to 191 (bench_pretrain on an A40 with this file reported n_params 9,557,760; grep finds no 'mtp' in pretrain.py). No pretraining-only parameters remain: pretraining trains exactly the 9,557,760 handed-off parameters (191 trained 11,433,344 including the 1,875,584-parameter MTP module)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; state_dict keys and shapes equal 191's
arch.kv_cache: unchanged code path (caches[0] holds key positions); forward is 189's, whose CPU check gave max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 between cached and full decoding; this session's bench sampled 4,096 proofs through the harness's KV-cache sampler without error

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on the 24 trunk hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms (unchanged from 191 except that the MTP module's matrices and LayerNorms no longer exist)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock from step 1, no warmup: lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget (setup and per-block compile included, so the first step runs at ~0.99 x peak after ~30-35 s), ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor. Unchanged from 191 (no warmup); with no MTP block to compile the first step runs ~5 s earlier (25 s in the bench)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1; MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same cosine fraction as AdamW from step 1, no warmup (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight: 25 Muon matrices (191: 30 with the MTP module's 5), captured as one CUDA graph as in 186/191
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters(), before both optimizers (191 clipped the joint norm of model + MTP module, so the trunk's share of the clip budget is now the whole)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight under Muon (25 matrices); emb.weight, biases and LayerNorms under AdamW; 9,557,760 parameters in total, all handed off

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged (the 200-step warmup those runs had is removed in 191, see optimizer.schedule). The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.compile: per-block torch.compile(dynamic=True) on the 6 trunk blocks (191: 7 with the MTP block), coalesce_tiling_analysis off, undone at handoff; Muon step as one CUDA graph; fused AdamW; batch max length from host
config.init: unchanged rule: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D trunk block parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0. Embedding and readout draw the same random numbers as in 191; the trunk's orthogonal matrices draw different ones (191 constructs the MTP module between building the trunk and the orthogonal-init loop)

loss.main: the fork's train.loss_on, called directly: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions, mean over those positions (identical to the `main` term of 191's mtp_loss; val_loss, train_loss and last_loss stay comparable with 129-191)
loss.total: main only; no auxiliary loss, no pretraining-only module

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence) on this pretrain.py, 2026-09-28 09:54-10:07 BST (590 s of that waiting for the pod): 797 steps in 60.3 s, first step at 25 s after setup and per-block compile, curve points 72 steps at 30 s, 441 at 45 s, 797 at 60 s, i.e. 24.2 steps/s from 30 to 60 s (191's bench: first step at 30 s, 20.8 steps/s; +16%), peak 7.43 GB, n_params 9,557,760, val loss 0.0846 at 60 s, sampling 168 samples/s on 4,096 samples (191's bench pod: 194), dynamo 2 unique graphs, torch 2.9.1+cu129; make -C code check clean
